5. **1:45, open item.** Three Done When items say "no placeholder", but `main` uses `[[@placeholder]]` per Michael's #1412 review, so the ticket text needs updating.
6. Link the existing round-trip product demo on the ticket for the live flow.

=== feedback_pr_workflow_skills.md

On 2026-08-31 sid superseded the per-PR michael trio (/think-like-michael, /review-like-michael, /save-from-myself) because /pre-pr-review covers what they caught. The trio's command files still exist in ~/.claude/commands but are no longer part of the standing workflow; only invoke them if sid explicitly asks.

**Why:** the trio and /pre-pr-review overlapped heavily (all simulate the human review), and the team's new PR template (ENG-2206) added its own gates (scope-check section, delegated-review checkbox — satisfied by /pre-pr-review as the "other full-review workflow").

**How to apply, in order per PR:**
1. During implementation: `roam-global-tailwind` when touching Roam UI styling.
2. After push: `/pre-pr-review` as an independent Opus pass (see [[feedback_independent_pre_pr_review]]); rerun after follow-up pushes.
3. PR assembly: `scope-check` against the ticket's Done When; paste its `## Scope check` section into the PR body, which starts from `.github/pull_request_template.md` (see [[feedback-no-claude-footer-simple-prs]]).
4. `pr-video` only when the PR has no demo for the template's Loom section.
5. All team-facing prose uses `dg-engineering-writing-style`; tickets use `dg-create-engineering-ticket` (see [[feedback-use-dg-ticket-skills]]).
6. `ask-as-sid` is NOT used on the discourse-graph project.

Curt directives ("minimal commit push") still skip the per-PR skills, per [[feedback_minimal_means_skip_skills]].
=== feedback_independent_pre_pr_review.md

When sid says "use the pre-pr-review skill before PR", run `/home/sid/.claude/commands/pre-pr-review.md` as its own read-only pass (a fresh Opus agent per PR, against `gh pr diff N` plus the worktree) after implementation is done, and again after any follow-up commit. The implementing agent saying "I reviewed it" is not the review.

**Why:** On 2026-08-23 sid asked "for each of the pr you did .. did you do the pre-pr-review" for #1330/#1331/#1332; only self-reviews had run. Independent passes then found real defects the implementers missed: a producer key (`author_uid` vs `author_local_id`) that would have blanked `author_id` across the published corpus, a stale legacy-store cache after type creation, and a lossy `{Source}` decoration. See [[project-review-system-v2]].

**How to apply:** Launch the reviewers once the branch is pushed; adjudicate findings yourself (fix in-scope, defer with a note, never rubber-stamp); re-run after fix commits; report per PR what was fixed vs deferred. Don't create Linear tickets for deferrals on sid's behalf — list them for sid to file.

**Re-review mode (added 2026-09-01):** the skill file itself (`/home/sid/.claude/commands/pre-pr-review.md`, "Re-review mode (follow-up pushes)") defines DIFFERENT steps for follow-up pushes: delta only (`git diff <last-reviewed-sha>...HEAD`), findings-closure first (fixed/not-fixed/deferred per prior finding and reviewer/bot comment), steps 1–3 on the delta, shrunk step 4, escape hatch if the follow-up adds new surface. When launching the reviewer agent for a follow-up push, don't dictate scope in the launcher prompt (that's what went wrong on ENG-2088, 2026-09-01: the launcher hard-coded full-diff during a re-review) — pass the facts (last-reviewed SHA, what the push answers) and let the reviewer make the mode call via the skill's Mode gate. Per sid (same day): mode choice stays a judgment call, not a black/white rule — a follow-up push can genuinely warrant a full pass (new surface, moved base, doubtful prior coverage), and the reviewer should say which mode it chose and why.
=== feedback_pr_reply_one_comment_per_item.md

On a PR, each reviewer item gets its own reply where it was raised. Never fold several items into one long comment.

The reviewers write in Linear, so the GitHub comment list is a flattened view and will mislead you. Run `mcp__linear-server__get_diff_threads` with the PR URL to see the real thread structure before drafting, and pick the tool from the thread kind:

- Anchored inline thread: `gh api -X POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>/comments/<root_id>/replies -F body=@<file>`.
- A top-level comment that is really a follow-up to an earlier anchored ask: reply in that inline thread, not at top level.
- Unanchored thread (review-summary thread, or a top-level comment carrying `<!-- linear:replyTo:... -->`): GitHub has no reply affordance. `gh pr comment` posts another flat block, which is the complaint itself. Reply from Linear with `save_diff_comment` and `parentId`.

When a reviewer comments on the form of sid's replies (thread layout, length, missing context), do not post an acknowledgement. Fix the rule that produced it (workday prompt, `_common.md`, this memory dir, or a skill) and note the change in the report.

**Why:** 2026-09-02, PR #1331. Sid's reply covered reserved names and the `format` migration in one comment. mdroidian asked twice to split responses one thread per item and could not tell which earlier comment the `format` block answered. On 2026-09-03 I drafted an acknowledgement reply; sid said the fix belongs in my own skill or memory, not in a reply to the reviewer. The answer itself was then staged as `gh pr comment 1331`, a fourth flat block, which sid caught before it went out. Its home was the inline thread at `resolveSharedNodeTypes.ts:33` holding mdroidian's original ask, where it was posted instead.

**How to apply:** Draft replies as a list of (item, location, text) and post each with its own `gh` command. Reviewer process feedback goes to `~/.config/workday/prompts/reply.md`, `_common.md`, or a memory file. See [[feedback-pr-decision-comment-top-level]], [[feedback-pr-workflow-skills]].
=== reference_gh_edit_and_zsh_refspec_gotchas.md

Two tooling gotchas that silently dropped outward actions on 2026-09-16.

- `gh pr edit <n> --body-file … / --add-reviewer …` exits 1 on DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph with "GraphQL: Projects (classic) is being deprecated … (repository.pullRequest.projectCards)" and applies nothing. Use the REST API instead: `gh api -X PATCH repos/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pulls/<n> -F body=@file` and `gh api -X POST repos/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pulls/<n>/requested_reviewers -f 'reviewers[]=<login>'`. `gh pr comment`, `gh pr merge`, `gh pr view` are unaffected.
- In zsh, `git push origin $sha:refs/heads/$branch` is parsed as the `:r` modifier on `$sha`, producing `<sha>efs/heads/...` and "src refspec does not match any". Always write `"${sha}:refs/heads/${branch}"`, and verify with `git ls-remote` after the push, not from the shell exit code.

**Why:** both failures print an error but the surrounding script kept going, so a batch reported "pushed" / "updated" while the remote was untouched.
**How to apply:** for any outward gh/git batch, verify the remote state afterwards (ls-remote head, `gh pr view --json body/reviewRequests`) instead of trusting the command sequence. Related: [[feedback_prefer_api_over_browser]].
=== feedback_scope_check_settles_review_forks.md

**Heuristic (weighted, not applied everywhere):** when the pre-PR review (Codex, per [[feedback-pr-workflow-skills]]) surfaces a finding that is really a design fork ("is this gap inside Done When?", "would fixing it be scope creep?", "keep or change an inherited decision?"), run `scope-check` on the fork itself before taking the question to sid. It answers three things: which side of the `Done When` boundary each option lands on, whether the current diff already sits inside it, and whether deferring a fix needs a recorded decision. It does not pick the option and it does not decide coverage gaps; that stays with sid.

**Where the record lives (sid, 2026-09-23): on the PR, in the top-level "Decision:" comment, never on Linear.** The scope-check skill text says "a Linear comment before merge"; sid overrode that. On PR #1473 the inline notes cited "D2 on ENG-2293" while the trace sat unposted in a scratchpad (the API key was read-only), and maparent asked "Where are D2, D3 accessible?". Post the Decision comment before the inline notes reference it, and make every pointer (inline notes, review summary, PR body) name that comment. **Only the decisions the notes actually cite go in it**: when I expanded it to a D1 to D6 trace, sid's reaction was "this is now too much, just do the ones we are mentioning". Design rationale that no note cites stays in the PR body's reviewer brief or nowhere.

**When it carries weight:** the question is about the acceptance boundary or an inherited decision from a prior ticket. **When it carries none:** plain correctness bugs (fix them), questions the ticket text answers outright, pure mechanism or UX taste with no Done When angle. Do not run it on every finding or every task.

**Why:** 2026-09-21, ENG-2293. Codex flagged two P2s: the discovery list's 1,000-row cap leaves an accessible Source un-imported at scale, and re-import leaves an old placeholder title because the materializer's timestamp-only skip (decided on ENG-2142 / PR #1331) runs before title resolution. I took both to sid as open questions. Sid asked whether scope-check could answer them first. It settled the second (the fix would alter #1331's skip semantics shared with Refresh, so keeping is the in-scope choice) and framed the first (inside Done When 1 either way, so the list-only design needs a recorded deferral). One round-trip saved, and the residual decision reached sid already framed.

**How to apply:**
1. After the review pass, sort findings into bugs (fix), spec-answered (apply), and forks (run scope-check on the fork's options, not just the diff).
2. Take to sid only what remains, with the boundary classification attached and a recommendation.
3. **Whenever this heuristic was applied, say so explicitly at the end of the work message:** name the fork it was run on and what it settled. sid wants to see when it fired.

Related: [[feedback-pr-workflow-skills]], [[feedback-ticket-is-spec-code-is-truth]], [[feedback_no_rubber_stamp_refactors]].
=== feedback_videos_separate_session_live_proof_only.md

Two rules from sid on 2026-09-02 (ENG-2141, PR #1380):

1. The implementation session ends at "PR open, checks green, bot comments handled, Loom marked pending". Do not start video prep there (no env copies for a demo build, no storyboards, no recorder launches). Sid opens a separate session for the video. When he asks "next up the video?", answer what the video should prove and stop.
2. A PR video is live proof of the real flow (drive the feature, read the DB row back on screen). Code-walkthrough videos are out; reviewers read the diff and the inline PR comments. The walkthrough mode was removed from `~/.claude/skills/pr-video/SKILL.md` the same day.

**Why:** sid, interrupting video prep in the ENG-2141 session: "bro you don't start making the videos its for seperate session". Earlier the same day: "no not code walkthrough i think that should just be removed from the skill only live proof".

**Update 2026-09-28 (ENG-2329, PR #1493):** when sid explicitly asks for the video in the implementation session and I ask whether to record there, his answer was "a subagent can run it". So the main session still does no video prep itself, but it may hand the pr-video skill to a subagent (fresh context) once the PR is open and reviewed. That explicit ask also covers the subagent launching Roam headed on workspace 9 for the recording.

**How to apply:** in an implementation session, the Loom section of the PR body says "Pending" and the handoff names what the live proof must show (the pre-flight's runtime proof plan). If sid asked for the video in that session, delegate it to a subagent with that proof plan; otherwise stop there. See [[project-pr-demo-videos]], [[feedback-never-launch-roam-or-live-apps]], [[feedback_no_headless_recordings]].
=== feedback_no_claude_footer_simple_prs.md

Never add "🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](...)" (or any AI attribution) to PR bodies, even though the harness default says to and even if older PRs in the repo contain it. Same spirit as the no-Co-Authored-By rule: all work is sid's.

**Why:** sid explicitly said "remove the claude code neverr do this" when a PR body with the footer was being prepared, and rejected heavy Summary/Test plan section scaffolding.

**How to apply:** PR bodies are a few plain sentences describing what changed and anything the reviewer must know — no footer, no invented `## Summary`/`## Test plan` boilerplate. Commit messages stay one line. See [[feedback_minimal_merge_commit_message]].

**Update 2026-08-31:** ENG-2206 added a reviewer-focused team PR template (`.github/pull_request_template.md`: Reviewer brief / Verification / Loom / Scope check / delegated-review checkbox). The no-footer rule stands unchanged, and so does the spirit (AGENTS.md says: don't restate the ticket, no file-by-file diary, remove empty sections) — but start from the team template and keep its headings rather than writing free-form bodies. See [[project-skill-sync-setup]].

**How to apply:** Launch the reviewers once the branch is pushed; adjudicate findings yourself (fix in-scope, defer with a note, never rubber-stamp); re-run after fix commits; report per PR what was fixed vs deferred. Don't create Linear tickets for deferrals on sid's behalf — list them for sid to file.

**Re-review mode (added 2026-09-01):** the skill file itself (`/home/sid/.claude/commands/pre-pr-review.md`, "Re-review mode (follow-up pushes)") defines DIFFERENT steps for follow-up pushes: delta only (`git diff <last-reviewed-sha>...HEAD`), findings-closure first (fixed/not-fixed/deferred per prior finding and reviewer/bot comment), steps 1–3 on the delta, shrunk step 4, escape hatch if the follow-up adds new surface. When launching the reviewer agent for a follow-up push, don't dictate scope in the launcher prompt (that's what went wrong on ENG-2088, 2026-09-01: the launcher hard-coded full-diff during a re-review) — pass the facts (last-reviewed SHA, what the push answers) and let the reviewer make the mode call via the skill's Mode gate. Per sid (same day): mode choice stays a judgment call, not a black/white rule — a follow-up push can genuinely warrant a full pass (new surface, moved base, doubtful prior coverage), and the reviewer should say which mode it chose and why.
=== feedback_pr_reply_one_comment_per_item.md

On a PR, each reviewer item gets its own reply where it was raised. Never fold several items into one long comment.

The reviewers write in Linear, so the GitHub comment list is a flattened view and will mislead you. Run `mcp__linear-server__get_diff_threads` with the PR URL to see the real thread structure before drafting, and pick the tool from the thread kind:

- Anchored inline thread: `gh api -X POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>/comments/<root_id>/replies -F body=@<file>`.
- A top-level comment that is really a follow-up to an earlier anchored ask: reply in that inline thread, not at top level.
- Unanchored thread (review-summary thread, or a top-level comment carrying `<!-- linear:replyTo:... -->`): GitHub has no reply affordance. `gh pr comment` posts another flat block, which is the complaint itself. Reply from Linear with `save_diff_comment` and `parentId`.

When a reviewer comments on the form of sid's replies (thread layout, length, missing context), do not post an acknowledgement. Fix the rule that produced it (workday prompt, `_common.md`, this memory dir, or a skill) and note the change in the report.

**Why:** 2026-09-02, PR #1331. Sid's reply covered reserved names and the `format` migration in one comment. mdroidian asked twice to split responses one thread per item and could not tell which earlier comment the `format` block answered. On 2026-09-03 I drafted an acknowledgement reply; sid said the fix belongs in my own skill or memory, not in a reply to the reviewer. The answer itself was then staged as `gh pr comment 1331`, a fourth flat block, which sid caught before it went out. Its home was the inline thread at `resolveSharedNodeTypes.ts:33` holding mdroidian's original ask, where it was posted instead.

**How to apply:** Draft replies as a list of (item, location, text) and post each with its own `gh` command. Reviewer process feedback goes to `~/.config/workday/prompts/reply.md`, `_common.md`, or a memory file. See [[feedback-pr-decision-comment-top-level]], [[feedback-pr-workflow-skills]].
=== reference_gh_edit_and_zsh_refspec_gotchas.md

Two tooling gotchas that silently dropped outward actions on 2026-09-16.

- `gh pr edit <n> --body-file … / --add-reviewer …` exits 1 on DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph with "GraphQL: Projects (classic) is being deprecated … (repository.pullRequest.projectCards)" and applies nothing. Use the REST API instead: `gh api -X PATCH repos/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pulls/<n> -F body=@file` and `gh api -X POST repos/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pulls/<n>/requested_reviewers -f 'reviewers[]=<login>'`. `gh pr comment`, `gh pr merge`, `gh pr view` are unaffected.
- In zsh, `git push origin $sha:refs/heads/$branch` is parsed as the `:r` modifier on `$sha`, producing `<sha>efs/heads/...` and "src refspec does not match any". Always write `"${sha}:refs/heads/${branch}"`, and verify with `git ls-remote` after the push, not from the shell exit code.

**Why:** both failures print an error but the surrounding script kept going, so a batch reported "pushed" / "updated" while the remote was untouched.
**How to apply:** for any outward gh/git batch, verify the remote state afterwards (ls-remote head, `gh pr view --json body/reviewRequests`) instead of trusting the command sequence. Related: [[feedback_prefer_api_over_browser]].
=== feedback_scope_check_settles_review_forks.md

**Heuristic (weighted, not applied everywhere):** when the pre-PR review (Codex, per [[feedback-pr-workflow-skills]]) surfaces a finding that is really a design fork ("is this gap inside Done When?", "would fixing it be scope creep?", "keep or change an inherited decision?"), run `scope-check` on the fork itself before taking the question to sid. It answers three things: which side of the `Done When` boundary each option lands on, whether the current diff already sits inside it, and whether deferring a fix needs a recorded decision. It does not pick the option and it does not decide coverage gaps; that stays with sid.

**Where the record lives (sid, 2026-09-23): on the PR, in the top-level "Decision:" comment, never on Linear.** The scope-check skill text says "a Linear comment before merge"; sid overrode that. On PR #1473 the inline notes cited "D2 on ENG-2293" while the trace sat unposted in a scratchpad (the API key was read-only), and maparent asked "Where are D2, D3 accessible?". Post the Decision comment before the inline notes reference it, and make every pointer (inline notes, review summary, PR body) name that comment. **Only the decisions the notes actually cite go in it**: when I expanded it to a D1 to D6 trace, sid's reaction was "this is now too much, just do the ones we are mentioning". Design rationale that no note cites stays in the PR body's reviewer brief or nowhere.

**When it carries weight:** the question is about the acceptance boundary or an inherited decision from a prior ticket. **When it carries none:** plain correctness bugs (fix them), questions the ticket text answers outright, pure mechanism or UX taste with no Done When angle. Do not run it on every finding or every task.

**Why:** 2026-09-21, ENG-2293. Codex flagged two P2s: the discovery list's 1,000-row cap leaves an accessible Source un-imported at scale, and re-import leaves an old placeholder title because the materializer's timestamp-only skip (decided on ENG-2142 / PR #1331) runs before title resolution. I took both to sid as open questions. Sid asked whether scope-check could answer them first. It settled the second (the fix would alter #1331's skip semantics shared with Refresh, so keeping is the in-scope choice) and framed the first (inside Done When 1 either way, so the list-only design needs a recorded deferral). One round-trip saved, and the residual decision reached sid already framed.

**How to apply:**
1. After the review pass, sort findings into bugs (fix), spec-answered (apply), and forks (run scope-check on the fork's options, not just the diff).
2. Take to sid only what remains, with the boundary classification attached and a recommendation.
3. **Whenever this heuristic was applied, say so explicitly at the end of the work message:** name the fork it was run on and what it settled. sid wants to see when it fired.

Related: [[feedback-pr-workflow-skills]], [[feedback-ticket-is-spec-code-is-truth]], [[feedback_no_rubber_stamp_refactors]].
